web_blocks.html: The Progressive Corporation (NYSE: PGR) is a `TIER_1` `CORE_ALPHA` compounder. It pairs the widest behavioral-data moat in U.S. P&C insurance with a strict 96.0% combined ratio cap [1, 10, 12]. From FY2016 to FY2025, net premiums earned grew from $22,474 million to $81,661 million, a 15.4% CAGR [1, 2]. Over that span, net income rose from $1,031 million to $11,308 million [1, 2]. In FY2025, operating cash flow hit $17,548 million, or 155.2% of net income, with a 35.3% ROE [1, 6]. In Q3 2026, policies in force grew 6% YoY to 40.489 million at an 88.7% combined ratio. Written and earned premium growth moderated to +4% and +5% YoY [3, 4].

At the November 16, 2026 close of $237.35 ($137.51 billion market cap), PGR trades at 11.95x trailing P/E, 14.67x forward P/E, and 3.99x book value [25]. We calibrate our Excess-Return model to Q3 2026 deceleration (5.5% NPE CAGR, 91.5% normalized combined ratio). That yields a **$262.00 Base fair value** (+10.4% vs. CMP). Against a **$205.00 invalidation stop** (below the $210.72 200-DMA), CMP offers only **0.76:1** reward-to-risk (`< 1.50:1`). It also sits above the $235.10 Street consensus in a `Correction` regime (6 index distribution days, 52.4% breadth, 4 PGR distribution days in 25 sessions) [25]. PGR therefore earns a **New-Capital Verdict of `WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT`**. On pullback into **$218.00–$226.27** (50-DMA $220.36 to 10-week EMA $226.27), R:R expands to **1.68:1**. Our **Holding Action is `NOT_HELD`**, with 0 shares across Schwab and Robinhood [25].

book_subsections.title: 0.1 Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict, and What to Do Today
paragraphs: Before diving into Progressive's 89-year history and ten-year ledger, let us put the conclusion up front. The Progressive Corporation (NYSE: PGR) is a Tier-1 Core Alpha compounder with a COMPOUNDER_PASS quality rating. Over the past decade, Progressive tripled net premiums earned from $22.474 billion to $81.661 billion. It grew net income tenfold to $11.308 billion and generated $17.548 billion in FY2025 operating cash flow. In Q3 2026, policies in force rose 6% year-over-year to 40.489 million at an 88.7% combined ratio. Meanwhile, premium growth cooled to 4% written and 5% earned.

At $237.35 per share, PGR trades at 11.95x trailing earnings, 14.67x forward earnings, and 3.99x book value. That price sits above the $235.10 Wall Street consensus target. We model a realistic 5.5% NPE growth rate and a 91.5% normalized combined ratio. Those inputs yield a $262.00 Base target, or +10.4% above market. Across Bull ($305.00, 25%), Base ($262.00, 50%), and Bear ($190.00, 25%) cases, our expected value is $254.75 (+7.3%).

Look closely at the risk math at market today. Upside to $262.00 is $24.65 per share, while downside to our $205.00 stop is $32.35 per share. That gives just 0.76-to-1 asymmetry at CMP, well below our 1.50-to-1 hurdle. Progressive also logged four distribution days in 25 sessions while the U.S. market sits in a Correction regime. That combination earns a WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT verdict.

We initiate zero equity or options exposure at $237.35. In our 100%-reconciled US cash plan, we keep 75% in CASH as dry powder. We allocate 25% to shortlist pick AVPT to diversify away from P&C insurance. We stage a 50% PGR entry only on a pullback into $218.00–$226.27, where reward-to-risk reaches 1.68-to-1 against a $205.00 hard stop. Great compounders reward patience when entry math is thin.

In the chapters ahead, we walk through Progressive's 89-year operating playbook, its Snapshot telematics moat, and its ten-year financial ledger. You will see why Q3 2026 policy growth to 40.489 million policies confirms durable share gains, even as premium growth cools to 4%–5%. We also audit CEO Tricia Griffith's five-year execution record and stress-test every valuation assumption. Keep Progressive at the top of your watchlist, set your limit alerts at $226.27 and $220.36, and let the market bring the price to you.
